newsitem.title: BOTSWANA: Bank of Botswana ups income 50 percent in 1996.
newsitem.headline: Bank of Botswana ups income 50 percent in 1996.

text.p: The Bank of Botswana reported a 50 percent increase in its income for the calendar year 1996 from 1995 on Wednesday.
The net income of the bank, primarily derived from earnings on the investment of Botswana's foreign exchange reserves, was 1.13 billion pula compared to 750 million in 1995.

The payout to government, which took 95 percent of the bank's net income plus 10 percent of the balance of the revaluation of Botswana's foreign reserves due to currency fluctuations, was 1.70 billion pula, up from 1.05 billion the previous year.
During 1996, the international reserves, including 239 million pula in assets held with the International Monetary Fund (IMF), increased by 35.7 percent to 18.34 billion pula.
However, 3.35 billion of this increase was a result of the depreciation of the pula against the major currencies in which the international reserves are held.
Deposit liabilities of the bank increased by 1.6 billion pula, equal to 18.8 percent, over the year.

The bank attributed this mostly to increases in government deposits with the bank, up by 11.5 percent, and Bank of Botswana Certificates (BoBCs) used by the bank to mop up excess liquidity in the banking system, which went up by 852 million pula (43.4 percent).
As at December 31, 1996, government deposits were 7.20 billion pula.
